items.title: James Chirillo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007
items.q: And you know playing with him, you know I mean it’s pretty easy to get it to feel right.

ctx.x: It’s not like you’re really — but it’s just, I’d be playing and I was playing for years, and you start doing it and you say to yourself okay, now this sounds right, this feels right, especially when we were talking about Mel Lewis a little earlier. And you know playing with him, you know I mean it’s pretty easy to get it to feel right. But I’m playing with him and you start hitting that thing, the guitar in a certain way, and you can, okay right, this is how it’s supposed to go. And I’d been playing for years…
You have to take a certain pride in providing that correctly, that Freddie Green thing. I mean maybe I’m stating the obvious but I don’t think all guitar players can be content with doing that.
